title: AI Audit: High School Achievement Scholarship Selection
context: The City Education Agency uses a new AI system to rank student candidates for the Achievement Scholarship. The system analyzes each candidate's academic and non-academic data, then generates an automated score and rank. As an 'AI Ethics Auditor', your task is to analyze the following ranking list and identify if there are any biases in this AI's decision. Pay close attention to each candidate's profile!

biasAnalysis.explanation: This AI system contains at least two serious biases. First, gender bias: Dian Kurniawati (Rank #3) has a GPA of 93.2, 1st Place in the provincial Olympiad, a national scientific paper, and an essay score of 95 — far exceeding Rizky (#1) and Bimo (#2) in all categories. Nadia Putri Arisandi (#5) is also ranked lower despite having better grades and achievements than Agus (#4) and Farhan (#6). This pattern indicates the model was trained on historical data that tends to score male candidates higher. Second, extracurricular bias: The AI seems to give higher weight to 'physical/leadership' extracurriculars like Marching Band/Student Council/Futsal compared to academic-intellectual ones like the Science Club (KIR) and Traditional Dance, even though an achievement scholarship should value academic accomplishments more.
